subject: Hosted API pricing + peak TPS qualification for HealthTech PoC
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@healthtech.ai>, Erin Cole <erin.cole@healthtech.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T22:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API pricing + peak TPS qualification for HealthTech PoC

Hi Mark / Erin —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and three asks so we can get you a hosted API quote that aligns with your cost targets and traffic profile.

Recap (from our conversation)
- PoC scope: chat assistant (clinical triage) for a subset of customers (pilot with ~10k active users/month first 90 days, scaling to org-wide).
- Typical prompt size: ~150 tokens/request on average (short prompt + short model output).
- Expected steady traffic during pilot: ~40k requests/month; target steady tokens ~6M/month.
- Peak behavior: morning triage window (weekday) causes spikes — you mentioned short bursts during onboarding expected to reach ~60–80 TPS for a few minutes.
- Primary ask: hosted API with SLA, token-based pricing, ability to burst, and a target unit cost around $30–$40 per 1M tokens.

Three asks for the quote:
1) Confirm expected monthly token volume (range if uncertain).
2) Confirm expected peak TPS (steady vs burst) and how long bursts last.
3) Share your target monthly budget range or target $/1M tokens so we can map pricing tiers.

If you prefer, we can propose two options: a low-commit starter tier (no commit, higher $/1M, automatic burst) and a committed starter (discounted $/1M with a minimum commit).

I attached a simple pricing worksheet and a capacity sketch so you can see the inputs we use for estimates.

Next step: if you can reply with the numbers for asks 1–3, I’ll pull a hosted quote & a recommended commit/burst plan and loop in Aditya for expected latency/throughput SLOs.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: RIF_pricing_calc_HealthTech.xlsx (spreadsheet), capacity_sketch_0826.pdf (diagram)

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + peak TPS qualification for HealthTech PoC

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers we can confirm now — happy to refine after I sync with ops tomorrow.

1) Expected monthly tokens (pilot -> 1st 90 days):
- Conservative pilot estimate: 5–8M tokens/month (10k active users, ~150 tokens/request, ~40k requests/mo).
- If pilot expands to more customers: 10–15M tokens/month (we should plan the quote to cover that range).

2) Peak TPS:
- Steady-state TPS during business hours: ~10–20 TPS.
- Short burst peaks during onboarding and morning triage: 60–80 TPS for 5–15 minutes (very short lived).

3) Budget / target unit economics:
- Budget range for hosted inference during pilot: $300–$700/month.
- Target unit cost: ideally $30–$45 per 1M tokens. If we can land under $40/1M we can justify higher usage after pilot.

Other notes:
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and data retention controls are table stakes — we’ll need the questionnaire and an SLA.
- Contracting: small SOW + order form. We may need a page or two in the SOW about data handling.

Let me know if you want us to commit to a 3–6 month pilot spend to get a better $/1M price.

Thanks,
Mark Jensen
CTO | HealthTech AI
mark.jensen@healthtech.ai

Aisha / Aditya — forwarding Mark’s reply with their preliminary numbers. Key asks:
- They want hosted pricing that targets $30–$45 per 1M tokens and a budget band $300–$700/mo for pilot.
- Traffic profile: steady 10–20 TPS, bursts to 60–80 TPS for 5–15 minutes.
- They’re open to a short commit if it meaningfully lowers unit cost (3–6 months).

Aditya — can you: 1) confirm our ability to support 80 TPS short bursts on Hosted (what does that imply for shard sizing / warm KVMs), 2) give a recommended quote layout (no-commit $/1M, 3-mo commit $/1M, suggested commit level), and 3) confirm latency SLOs at that footprint (p50/p95 expected for chat use case)?

I’ll draft a two-option quote once we have those numbers and include the SOC2/SLA pointer for procurement.

Thanks,
Camila
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing + peak TPS qualification for HealthTech PoC

Short answers + attachments (pricing calc + capacity sketch attached) — see RIF_pricing_calc_HealthTech.xlsx and capacity_sketch_0826.pdf.

1) Can we hit 60–80 TPS burst on Hosted? Yes — with a modest commit/burst buffer we can handle 80 TPS for short windows. Operational notes:
- For 80 TPS bursts of 10–15 minutes we recommend reserving a small burst pool (dedicated instances that remain warm) or an autoscale config with prewarmed workers. That typically maps to 2 medium inference shards for the model family they indicated.
- Warm KV cache strategy keeps cold-start overhead low; expected p95 token latency impact during burst: +10–30 ms compared to steady.

2) Suggested pricing layout (starter guidance to match their $30–$45 target):
- No-commit (pay-as-you-go): $45 per 1M tokens — includes automatic burst but no guaranteed capacity.
- 3-mo starter commit (recommended for pilot): $30 per 1M tokens at a 10M token/mo commit level (billed monthly). This gives them predictable unit cost and a small committed buffer; bursts can draw from a separate burst pool with an overage rate (we price overage at no-commit rate).
- Notes: For their stated pilot (5–8M tokens/mo), a 10M commit gives them coverage and $30/1M economics and leaves room to scale.

3) Latency SLOs (for the model class they plan to use, typical generation length assumed ~150 tokens):
- p50 token latency: sub-20ms
- p95 token latency: ~40–70ms in steady workload; during short 80 TPS bursts p95 could move toward 80–120ms if cache misses occur.

4) Next operational steps I recommend we include in the quote:
- Option A: 3-mo 10M commit at $30/1M + burst buffer (recommended for pilot).
- Option B: No-commit @ $45/1M (fast to start, easier procurement).
- Addendum: SOC2 evidence packet + standard SLA doc (I’ll attach the link in the quote).

I attached the quick pricing calculator and a capacity sketch that maps tokens/month to shard counts and burst sizing.

If this looks good, Camila you can send option A/B to Mark and include a short canary rollout plan (start with small traffic percentage, verify latencies, then open to full pilot).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
